citation: 'Water Tower, Chicago Ave & Drive, 1890', photograph, ca. 1890. Chicago History Museum, ICHi-05902.
author: Unknown photographer
repository: Chicago History Museum, ICHi-05902, shown on The Great Chicago Fire and the Web of Memory's Water Tower page. Not committed to this repository.
locator: Taken from high up south-west of the tower, across Chicago Avenue: the tower in its grounds, a lawn with walks and young trees inside a low stone kerb with an iron railing along Chicago Avenue and down its west side, the pumping works behind across Pine Street, and houses beyond the grounds to the north-west.
rights_note: An unpublished photograph of about 1890 by an unknown photographer, more than 120 years old. Read for layout only; nothing is traced or sampled from it.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-21 (T-3689) from the Web of Memory's 920-pixel copy of ICHi-05902.
note: After the fire, so it is used only where it agrees with the 1866-67 lithograph and Greene's 1871 stereograph: open grounds round the tower, fenced on Chicago Avenue and on the west.
what_it_supplies: the tower's grounds as a fenced lawn reaching west of the tower and north toward Pearson Street
